items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Myra Melford who I was hanging out with last night or Marilyn Crispell, Maria Schneider

ctx.x: And they feel like — I don’t know to me that sounds like an excuse. This is a music that comes out of an African-American basis. I’ve thought of it as an African-American gift to the world. And there’s always been very strong white musicians back to Adrian Rollini up to Steve Lacy, Tim Berne, Dave Douglas, Myra Melford who I was hanging out with last night or Marilyn Crispell, Maria Schneider, or middle aged white guys I mean there are a lot of players who are quite strong. Marty Erlich, somebody who I enjoy…

playing a music that comes from an African-American basis? What does it mean to be middle aged and to be devoted to an art form that seems to be giving back very little in the way of monetary support? What distinguishes my work from his work, whether he’s black, white, purple, Latin, whatever. And I think that those are difficult challenges that we have to face but I think that it’s an excuse to say well I’m white and I’m middle aged so nobody cares about me. Well then make me care about you, you know? Tell me…
